svg.text: The 5-state champion is a counter that halts the first time n ≡ 2 (mod 3)
One round, every step drawn: a block of 37 ones becomes a block of 67
time runs left to right (937 steps); the tape runs top (left end) to bottom (right end); dark = 1, white = 0
head in state B, sweeping right through the block
head in state D, sweeping back left
turning points (states A, C, E) are single steps
end: 67 ones, and the next round starts
The whole run: 15 rounds, each starting from a solid block of n ones
log scale; a straight line means growth by a constant factor (5/3 per round). Colour = n mod 3.
12,287 ≡ 2: the machine sweeps left for 12,289 more steps and halts
From n ones the machine reaches the next block after (5n² + 33n + 45)/9 steps if n ≡ 0, or (5n² + 41n + 71)/9 if n ≡ 1 (mod 3); if n ≡ 2 it halts after n + 2 steps.
I fitted these constants on the champion's own orbit, then ran the machine from every block n = 1…250: 250 of 250 matched exactly.
The orbit 3 → 9 → 19 → … → 12,287 then reproduces S = 47,176,870 and Σ = 4,098. Verified by simulation, not proved for all n by this code.
Why it is a lottery win: of the first million starting blocks, 0.343% survive 14 rounds, and (2/3)^14 = 0.343%. This start dodged residue 2 fourteen times.
